{{Update|date=July 2021}}
'''Sun Jie''' ({{zh|s=孙杰|p=Sūn Jié}}, born 13 June 1988 in [[Fuyang, Zhejiang|Fuyang]], [[Hangzhou]], [[Zhejiang]]) is a male [[PR China|Chinese]] [[rowing (sport)|rower]], who competed for [[China at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Team China]] at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]] and the [[2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/su/sun-jie-1.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417184934/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/su/sun-jie-1.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Sun Jie Bio, Stats, and Results|website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref>  He competed in the men's lightweight sculls at both Olympics.  His teammate in 2008 was [[Zhang Guolin]], and they finished in 5th place.<ref name=":0" />  In 2012 his teammate was Zhang Fangbing, they finished in 15th place.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=IOC|title=London 2012 lightweight double sculls 2x men Results - Olympic rowing|url=https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/london-2012/rowing/lightweight-double-sculls-2x-men|access-date=2021-07-01|website=Olympic Channel|language=en}}</ref>

Since 2005, he has competed in world rowing events.<ref>{{Cite web|title=World Rowing - Jie SUN|url=https://worldrowing.com//athlete/fe4414f7-061c-452a-aba3-f568aa3c1606|access-date=2021-07-01|website=World Rowing|language=en}}</ref> Although, he primarily competes in Lightweight Men's Double Sculls, he competed in the Chinese men's lightweight eight at the [[2010 World Rowing Championships|2010 World Championships]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.worldrowing.com/athletes/athlete/22905/results/|title=Jie SUN - worldrowing.com|website=www.worldrowing.com|language=en-US|access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> 

==Major performances==
*2006 National Spring Champions Tournament – 1st LM1X;
*2006 National Championships – 1st LM1X;
*2007 World Cup, Netherlands – 7th LM2X;
*2007 World Championships – 9th LM2X;
*2008 World Cup, Munich – 4th LM2X;
*2008 Olympics, Beijing - 5th LM2X;
*2012 Olympics, Great Britain - 15th LM2X
